overview.intro: Elections are the machinery through which a democracy obtains the consent of the governed. This chapter explains what elections mean, the composition and functions of the Election Commission of India which conducts them, the difference between direct and indirect elections, and the three kinds of elections held in India - general, mid-term and by-elections.

blocks.text: Democracy means government by consent, and consent is expressed through regular, free and fair elections. In India the Constitution (Article 324) provides for the superintendence, direction and control of elections by an Election Commission, first appointed in 1950, so that no government in power can manipulate the polls. Since the first general election of 1951-52, India has run one of the largest election exercises in the world using universal adult franchise.

Meaning and importance of elections. An election is the recognised method by which people choose their representatives to legislate and govern. Elections make the government accountable: rulers must return to the people at fixed intervals. They provide peaceful change of government, allow citizens to judge the performance of parties, and give legitimacy to authority.

Election Commission of India - composition. The Election Commission is a permanent, independent constitutional body. Since 1993 it consists of a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners, appointed by the President. They have a tenure of six years, or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, and can be removed like judges of the Supreme Court to keep the Commission free from executive pressure. The Commission has its own secretariat.

Election Commission - functions. The Commission superintends, directs and controls all elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. It prepares and revises electoral rolls, announces election schedules, allots symbols to political parties, enforces the Model Code of Conduct, appoints returning and presiding officers, keeps an eye on election expenses, cancels polls where they were not free and fair, and advises the President or Governor on disqualification of members.

Direct election. In a direct election, the voters themselves elect the representative. Members of the Lok Sabha and of State Legislative Assemblies are chosen this way from territorial constituencies on the basis of universal adult franchise. Direct elections keep representatives closely answerable to the people, but they are expensive and demand an informed electorate.

Indirect election. In an indirect election, the people's chosen representatives elect someone further. The President of India is elected by an Electoral College of elected MPs and MLAs; members of State Legislative Councils and of the Rajya Sabha are elected by MLAs. Indirect election saves cost and suits offices needing experience rather than mass appeal, but it reduces the direct link with voters.

General election. A general election is the regular election held after every five years (the normal term of the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly) to constitute a new House. Candidates of many parties contest; the party or coalition that wins a majority forms the government.

Mid-term election. When a Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly is dissolved before completing its five-year term - for example, if no party can prove a majority - an election called a mid-term election is held to constitute a new House for the remaining period.

By-election. If a seat in the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly falls vacant mid-term, because of the death, resignation or disqualification of the member, a by-election is held in that one constituency only, and the winner serves for the unexpired term.

items: Election Commission of India - Permanent constitutional body (Article 324); CEC plus two Election Commissioners since 1993; independent of the government of the day.
Electoral College - Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of State Legislative Assemblies; elects the President (indirect election).
Returning and Presiding Officers - Public servants appointed by the Commission to conduct polling and counting at the constituency level.

blocks.text: Direct election vs Indirect election: Voters choose the representative themselves (Lok Sabha, Assembly) versus elected members choosing (President, Rajya Sabha).
General election vs Mid-term election: Held at the end of a normal five-year term versus held after premature dissolution of the House.
Mid-term election vs By-election: Election for a whole House after dissolution versus election for a single vacant seat within an existing House.

items: 1950 - Election Commission of India established under Article 324.
1951-52 - First general election on the basis of universal adult franchise.
1989 - 61st Amendment lowers voting age from 21 to 18 years.
1993 - Election Commission becomes a multi-member body: CEC plus two Election Commissioners.
1998 onwards - Photograph-bearing voter ID cards and, later, EVMs become standard across India.
New Delhi - headquarters of the Election Commission of India

blocks.text: Cause: Fear that a government in power could rig elections Effect: The Constitution created an independent Election Commission to conduct polls.
Cause: The need for stability in offices requiring experience Effect: President and Rajya Sabha members are chosen by indirect election.
Cause: Death, resignation or disqualification of a member Effect: A by-election is held in that constituency.
Cause: No party able to command a majority in the House Effect: The House may be dissolved and a mid-term election held.

items: Saying the Election Commission is appointed by Parliament - it is appointed by the President.
Confusing mid-term elections with by-elections: a mid-term election is for the whole House; a by-election is for one seat.
Writing that the President is directly elected - the election is indirect through the Electoral College.
Forgetting that the Model Code of Conduct is enforced by the Election Commission, not by the government.
Stating the voting age as 21 instead of 18.

questions.prompt: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing it with emergency or amendment articles.

questions.prompt: The President of India is elected by:
options: An Electoral College of elected MPs and MLAs
questions.answer: An Electoral College of elected MPs and MLAs
questions.explanation: The President's election is indirect, through elected members of Parliament and State Assemblies.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming the President is directly elected.

questions.prompt: An election held for one Lok Sabha seat after the member's death is called a:
questions.explanation: A by-election fills a single vacant seat; a mid-term election follows dissolution of the whole House.

questions.prompt: How many Election Commissioners serve on the Election Commission (since 1993)?
questions.answer: Three - the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
questions.explanation: It became a multi-member body in 1993.

questions.prompt: In which year was the voting age lowered to 18 years?
State any two functions of the Election Commission of India.
questions.answer: Any two of: preparing and revising electoral rolls; announcing election schedules; alloting symbols to parties and candidates; enforcing the Model Code of Conduct; appointing returning/presiding officers; scrutinising election expenses; advising the President/Governor on disqualifications; cancelling polls that were not free and fair.
questions.explanation: The Commission superintends, directs and controls all elections.
questions.commonMistake: Naming functions of Parliament or the government instead.

questions.prompt: Distinguish between a mid-term election and a by-election.
questions.answer: A mid-term election is held when the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly is dissolved before completing its five-year term, and it constitutes a new House. A by-election is held only for a single constituency whose seat falls vacant mid-term through death, resignation or disqualification; the winner serves the unexpired term.
questions.commonMistake: Treating the two as the same scale of election.

questions.prompt: Distinguish between direct and indirect elections, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: In direct election, voters themselves choose the representative by casting votes - e.g., elections to the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of universal adult franchise. In indirect election, the people's elected representatives choose the office-holder - e.g., the President of India, elected by an Electoral College of elected MPs and MLAs; members of Legislative Councils and the Rajya Sabha are also indirectly elected by MLAs. Direct election keeps representatives closely answerable to voters; indirect election saves cost and suits offices requiring experience.
questions.commonMistake: Mixing up the examples of each type.

questions.prompt: Give reasons: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only like a judge of the Supreme Court.
questions.answer: To keep the Commission independent of the government of the day. If the CEC could be dismissed at will, the ruling party could pressure the referee of elections; the judge-like removal (on proved misbehaviour or incapacity, by Parliament) protects impartial conduct of polls, fair rolls, symbols and the Model Code of Conduct.
questions.commonMistake: Stating the rule without the reason.

questions.prompt: Describe the composition of the Election Commission of India and explain how it ensures free and fair elections.
questions.answer: Composition: a permanent constitutional body under Article 324; since 1993 it consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners, appointed by the President, with a six-year tenure or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier; the CEC's removal is protected like a Supreme Court judge's. Ensuring free and fair polls: it prepares and revises electoral rolls so every eligible voter is listed; announces schedules so campaigning is orderly; allots symbols and recognises parties; enforces the Model Code of Conduct so ruling parties gain no unfair advantage; appoints returning, presiding and counting officers; monitors expenditure and spending limits; deploys central forces where needed; can countermand polls marred by rigging; and advises on disqualifications. Its independence, fixed tenure and wide powers make it the referee of Indian democracy.
questions.explanation: Composition + protective functions = a full answer.
questions.commonMistake: Listing composition without explaining the fairness mechanisms.

questions.prompt: A state government announces free laptops for voters a week before polling. What can the Election Commission do, and why?
questions.answer: The Commission enforces the Model Code of Conduct: it can halt such announcements, order postponement until after polling, and censure or act against officials who misuse government machinery. It acts because conduct of elections (Article 324) is in its hands, and paid announcements before polls can unduly influence voters - all parties must have a level field.
questions.explanation: Apply MCC powers to the scenario.
questions.commonMistake: Saying the government is free to announce schemes anytime.
